design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Signal proposal, promotion, and archive operations must be idempotent by stable signalId, signalVersion, and proposalId. Lifecycle transitions must use compare-and-set or equivalent expected-state checks, reject stale versions, fail closed on concurrent modification, and prevent two operators from silently promoting or archiving conflicting revisions. Promotion requires explicit operator approval and a satisfied validation/backtest gate.
forbidden_alternatives: Generating Java classes or Java source from SignalSpec YAML.
Bypassing SignalSpec validation during propose, promote, compile, or backtest.
Bypassing R-015 with a new ad hoc backtest executor.
Promoting any signal solely because validation, compilation, or backtest passed.
Adding notebook-only or Python-only authoring flows for R-016 acceptance.
Adding a new OLTP database, ORM-backed persistence layer, Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle for SignalSpec catalog state.
Patching dag-framework locally instead of using existing extension points.
Letting UI write directly to Redis, QuestDB, Parquet, SignalSpec persistence, or any historical store.
Embedding author provenance only in UI state instead of API opportunity payloads.
Mutating historical backtest records during promotion.
Bypassing existing FeatureNode primitives with a parallel signal execution engine.
hard_constraints: Reuse the existing R-015 deterministic backtest path.
Do not add Java code generation for authored signals.
Compile only to existing FeatureNode primitives.
Do not allow auto-promotion without human/operator approval.
Validator diagnostics must be actionable for unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, and unknown apiVersion.
Stale, invalid, archived, invariant-failed, or partially failed SignalSpec versions must be rejected before promotion and live ranking activation.
Promoted signals must contribute to live ranking and render author provenance in opportunities and UI surfaces.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.

QA roots own fixtures, smoke coverage, regression assertions, API tests, and UI tests.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Persist one durable catalog row per SignalSpec proposal/version with immutable signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, author, canonical raw YAML body, normalized metadata, validator diagnostics, lifecycle state, R-015 backtest run reference, trackRecord summary, body hash or equivalent invariant marker, created/updated timestamps, promoted/archived timestamps, and operator identity when applicable. Invalid, archived, partially failed, invariant-failed, and superseded specs remain queryable but cannot contribute to live ranking.
design_contract.public_api: Expose SignalSpec v1 as declarative YAML plus /api/signals/propose, /api/signals/catalog, /api/signals/{signalId}, /api/signals/{signalId}/promote, and /api/signals/{signalId}/archive endpoints. Responses must surface validator diagnostics, immutable proposal/spec identifiers, lifecycle status, author provenance, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, operator approval state, archive state, and trackRecord. Opportunity and explainability payloads must include author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, and trackRecord for promoted signal contributions.

Persistence and lifecycle coverage: one row per SignalSpec proposal/version stores raw YAML, author, proposalId, signalId, signalVersion, diagnostics, lifecycle status, R-015 run id, trackRecord, invariant marker, and operator approval audit fields.
UI/API contract coverage: /api/signals/propose, catalog, get, promote, and archive responses match UI expectations; catalog and opportunities render author and trackRecord without fallback fields.
Configured QA gate coverage: qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh pass after targeted platform-dsl, app-api, and UI test suites.
assumptions: specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md is the frozen source of truth for SignalSpec v1 schema, lifecycle, validator rules, and authoring API semantics.
R-015 backtest execution is already available and must be reused rather than replaced or duplicated.
SignalSpec v1 compiles only to existing FeatureNode primitives and does not generate Java source code.
Promotion to live ranking is an explicit operator action and must be idempotent, auditable, and never automatic.
QA should front-load failing fixtures and tests under the registered QA write paths, then implementation slices make them pass.

acceptance_tests: equities.relativeVolumeZ.v1 fixture round-trips propose, validate, compile, backtest, promote, catalog/get, and live ranking contribution.
Validator rejects unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, and unknown apiVersion with field/path-specific diagnostics.
Promoted opportunities expose author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, and trackRecord.
Stale, invalid, invariant-mismatched, archived, and partially failed specs cannot be promoted or ranked.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Signal lifecycle transitions are serialized by signalId plus signalVersion or proposalId using conditional status updates. promote and archive are idempotent when repeated with the same expected state, reject stale versions, and fail closed on concurrent modification. Promotion requires explicit operator approval and a satisfied backtest/review gate.
forbidden_alternatives: Generating or compiling Java source from SignalSpec YAML.
Bypassing R-015 with a new ad hoc backtest executor.
Promoting a signal directly from propose or validate without operator approval.
Treating unknown fields, ops, refs, or apiVersion values as warnings when they affect execution semantics.
Embedding author provenance only in UI state instead of API opportunity payloads.
Mutating historical backtest records during promotion.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals.
Do not allow auto-promotion without human/operator approval.
Reuse the R-015 backtest path for deterministic evaluation.
Compile only to existing FeatureNode primitives.
Validator diagnostics must be actionable for unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, and unknown apiVersion.
Stale or invalid SignalSpec versions must be rejected before promotion.
Metadata/YAML invariant mismatch or body-hash failure must reject promotion and live ranking activation.
Partial backtest, persistence, or promotion failure must leave the signal non-live and retriable or archived without corrupting catalog state.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl owns SignalSpec parsing, validation diagnostics, cycle/ref resolution, and compilation to existing FeatureNode primitives. app-api owns authoring endpoints, persistence rows, YAML body storage, lifecycle transitions, and R-015 backtest orchestration. app-core/platform-runtime own promoted-signal contribution into live ranking and opportunity provenance publication. ui owns catalog, review, track-record, and provenance rendering. qa paths own fixtures, smoke coverage, regression assertions, and Playwright/API test gates.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Persist one row per SignalSpec proposal/version with immutable signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, author, raw YAML body, normalized metadata, validator diagnostics, lifecycle state, R-015 backtest run reference, trackRecord summary, body hash or equivalent invariant marker, created/updated timestamps, promoted/archived timestamps, and operator identity when applicable. Invalid, archived, partially failed, and superseded specs remain queryable but cannot contribute to live ranking.
design_contract.public_api: Expose SignalSpec v1 as declarative YAML plus /api/signals/propose, /api/signals/catalog, /api/signals/{signalId}, /api/signals/{signalId}/promote, and /api/signals/{signalId}/archive endpoints. The compiler public surface accepts a validated SignalSpec and returns an executable FeatureNode graph descriptor. Opportunity/explainability payloads must include author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, and trackRecord for promoted signal contributions.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Signal proposal, promotion, and archive operations must be idempotent by stable signalId, signalVersion, and proposalId. Lifecycle transitions must use expected-state compare-and-set or equivalent checks, reject stale proposal/version mutations, fail closed on concurrent modification, and prevent conflicting promote/archive operations from silently succeeding. Promotion requires explicit operator approval plus satisfied validation and R-015 backtest gates.
forbidden_alternatives: Generating Java classes or Java source from SignalSpec YAML.
Bypassing SignalSpec validation during propose, promote, compile, or backtest.
Bypassing R-015 with a new ad hoc backtest executor.
Promoting any signal solely because validation, compilation, or backtest passed.
Adding notebook-only or Python-only authoring flows for R-016 acceptance.
Adding a new OLTP database, ORM-backed persistence layer, Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle for SignalSpec catalog state.
Letting UI write directly to Redis, QuestDB, SignalSpec persistence, or any historical store.
Embedding author provenance only in UI state instead of API opportunity payloads.
Mutating historical backtest records during promotion.
Bypassing existing FeatureNode primitives with a parallel signal execution engine.
hard_constraints: Reuse the existing R-015 deterministic backtest path.
Do not add Java code generation for signals.
Compile only to existing FeatureNode primitives.
Do not allow auto-promotion without human/operator approval.
Validator diagnostics must be actionable for unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, and unknown apiVersion.
Stale, invalid, archived, invariant-failed, or partially failed SignalSpec versions must be rejected before promotion and live ranking activation.
Promoted signals must contribute to live ranking and render author provenance in opportunities and UI surfaces.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.

QA roots own fixtures, API tests, UI tests, smoke coverage, and regression assertions.

assumptions: specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md is the frozen source of truth for SignalSpec v1 schema, lifecycle, validator rules, and authoring API semantics.
R-015 deterministic backtest execution is already merged and must be reused rather than duplicated.
SignalSpec v1 compiles only to existing FeatureNode primitives and must not generate Java source code.
Promotion to live ranking is an explicit human/operator action and must be idempotent, auditable, and never automatic.
SignalSpec definitions are YAML-backed and persist as one durable row per SignalSpec version plus canonical YAML body without adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, Drizzle, or another OLTP store.

app-api may expose workflow endpoints and orchestrate the control-plane flow, but any durable write path must be documented as an R-016 control-plane exception or delegated to an existing non-web ownership surface so the Redis hot-view and historical-store split is not silently violated.
QA must author failing fixtures and tests under registered QA write paths before implementation slices make them pass.

Validator rejects unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, unknown apiVersion, malformed YAML, duplicate signalVersion, stale proposalId, and archived promotion attempts with actionable diagnostics tied to the offending field or spec location.
Promoted opportunities expose author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, and trackRecord.
Stale, invalid, invariant-mismatched, archived, and partially failed specs cannot be promoted or ranked.

qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh pass after implementation.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Signal proposal, promotion, and archive operations must be idempotent by stable signalId, signalVersion, and proposalId. Lifecycle transitions must use compare-and-set or equivalent expected-state checks, reject stale versions, fail closed on concurrent modification, and prevent two operators from silently promoting or archiving conflicting revisions. Promotion requires explicit operator approval and a satisfied validation/backtest gate.
forbidden_alternatives: Generating Java classes or Java source from SignalSpec YAML.
Bypassing SignalSpec validation during propose, promote, compile, or backtest.
Bypassing R-015 with a new ad hoc backtest executor.
Promoting any signal solely because validation, compilation, or backtest passed.
Adding notebook-only or Python-only authoring flows for R-016 acceptance.
Adding a new OLTP database, ORM-backed persistence layer, Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle for SignalSpec catalog state.
Letting UI write directly to Redis, QuestDB, Parquet, SignalSpec persistence, or any historical store.
Embedding author provenance only in UI state instead of API opportunity payloads.
Mutating historical backtest records during promotion.
Bypassing existing FeatureNode primitives with a parallel signal execution engine.
hard_constraints: Reuse the existing R-015 deterministic backtest path.
Do not add Java code generation for authored signals.
Compile only to existing FeatureNode primitives.
Do not allow auto-promotion without human/operator approval.
Validator diagnostics must be actionable for unknown op, unknown ref, cyclic transform, missing required field, and unknown apiVersion.
Stale, invalid, archived, invariant-failed, or partially failed SignalSpec versions must be rejected before promotion and live ranking activation.
Promoted signals must contribute to live ranking and render author provenance in opportunities and UI surfaces.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl owns SignalSpec parsing, validation diagnostics, cycle/ref resolution, apiVersion gating, and compilation to existing FeatureNode primitives. app-api owns HTTP DTOs, endpoint semantics, request authorization shape, and workflow orchestration but must not silently introduce a generic app-api DB ownership model. SignalSpec catalog durability must be either an explicit R-016 control-plane persistence exception recorded in specs/docs or delegated to app-core/platform-runtime control-plane code. app-core and platform-runtime own promoted-signal contribution into live ranking and opportunity provenance publication. ui owns catalog, review, promotion/archive controls, trackRecord, diagnostics, and provenance rendering. QA roots own fixtures, smoke coverage, regression assertions, API tests, and UI tests.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Persist one durable catalog row per SignalSpec proposal/version with immutable signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, author, canonical raw YAML body, normalized metadata, validator diagnostics, lifecycle state, R-015 backtest run reference, trackRecord summary, body hash or equivalent invariant marker, created/updated timestamps, promoted/archived timestamps, and operator identity when applicable. Invalid, archived, partially failed, invariant-failed, and superseded specs remain queryable but cannot contribute to live ranking.
design_contract.public_api: Expose SignalSpec v1 as declarative YAML plus /api/signals/propose, /api/signals/catalog, /api/signals/{signalId}, /api/signals/{signalId}/promote, and /api/signals/{signalId}/archive endpoints. Responses must surface validator diagnostics, immutable proposal/spec identifiers, lifecycle status, author provenance, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, operator approval state, archive state, and trackRecord. Opportunity and explainability payloads must include author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, and trackRecord for promoted signal contributions.
